newsitem.title: UK: Think-tank calls for Europe infrastructure agency.
newsitem.headline: Think-tank calls for Europe infrastructure agency.

text.p: A new European infrastructure agency is needed to overcome the obstacles to Trans-European Networks for transport, energy and telecommunications, the Federal Trust, an independent think-tank, said on Friday. "Modernising Europe's infrastructure is a key element in boosting competitiveness," the London-based Federal Trust said. "At present neither the quantity of public sector finance nor the quality of public authority management is sufficient to network Europe."
It added the European Union's aim of establishing priority Trans-European Networks (TENs) in large-scale infrastructure was unlikely to become a reality in the original time-scale.

"The difficulties facing the priority projects flow from their trans-frontier nature, their large scale, the high risk involved, their limited financial viability and the lack of political will," the think-tank said.

It emphasized the importance of public-private partnerships in providing both finance and expertise for the TENs, and called on the European Commission to establish a new task force charged with the speedy implementation of the projects and with galvanising such partnerships.

That task force, together with the already established High-Level Group, should prepare for a European Infrastructure Agency with power to evaluate and coordinate TENs projects from a European dimension, the Federal Trust said.
